investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Evals (remote-agent-state, remote-agent-create, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-state, remote-agent-create, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-22T12:26Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api's POST /api/agents call could not reach the swarm backend ELB at /v1/agents. Because the failure occurs at agent creation — before any state polling or runtime interaction can happen — no required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever collected, causing the expected-output contract to be fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting /v1/agents) was unreachable from the production-api at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check calls createAgent as its first step (evidenced by run-status-probes.mjs line 1905: `const agent = await createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId)`), so a gateway-level failure at POST /v1/agents causes all three sibling checks to fail immediately with the same 502 bad_gateway message before any evidence can be written. This is an eval-observed infrastructure connectivity failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty — zero fields written, confirming the probe never progressed past the createAgent call
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are absent, consistent with failure before any evidence could be recorded
sibling.remote-agent-create: same 502 message, latencyMs=11344, evidenceKeys=[]
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same 502 message, latencyMs=10914, evidenceKeys=[]

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1897-1905: runner calls createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId) at line 1905 — the first async operation after token and orgId checks, confirming the 502 is thrown at agent creation before state polling begins

verifierContext.siblingCorrelation.likelySharedDependencyFailure: true — all failing sibling IDs share the same message, pointing to a single shared upstream dependency rather than independent check-level bugs
possibleCauses: Primary: The swarm ELB (us-east-2) was down, misconfigured, or had no healthy targets at the time of the eval run, causing the production-api to receive a connection error when forwarding POST /v1/agents.
Secondary: A network policy, security-group rule, or VPC routing change between the production-api and the swarm ELB blocked outbound requests to the ELB endpoint at the time of the run.
Tertiary: The swarm service itself (behind the ELB) was restarting, scaled to zero, or had all instances fail their health checks, causing the ELB to return 502 with no healthy backend.

Lower confidence: A transient DNS or TLS resolution failure for the ELB hostname caused the connection attempt to fail; this would be consistent with the ~11-second latency seen across all three checks before the error was returned (failed-check.timing: latencyMs=11074).

investigation.title: published-observability-snapshot Eval Failure: Stale GitHub Actions Snapshot (snapshotAgeMinutes=715, max=300)
investigation.summary: The eval for the published-observability-snapshot check failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json is 715 minutes old, exceeding the contract maximum of 300 minutes. This is an eval-layer failure scoped to the snapshot freshness assertion; all sibling public-website checks passed, and there is no evidence of a user-facing outage.
investigation.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not run successfully in at least 715 minutes (approximately 11 hours 55 minutes). The contract requires snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300 (5 hours). The snapshot itself is structurally valid and carries a live source attribution, but its timestamp is too old to satisfy the freshness assertion. The most likely cause is that the scheduled or triggered GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the snapshot either failed silently, was skipped, or was not triggered during the expected window. This is an eval failure against the published snapshot's freshness; it is not a public website availability outage.
proof: failed-check.message: 'snapshotAgeMinutes expected <= 300 but got 715' — the sole violated assertion in the contract (evidenceItems: failed-check.message).

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=715, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true — the snapshot is structurally present and attributed to github-actions but is stale by 415 minutes (evidenceItems: failed-check.evidence).

expected-output.contract: assertion { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } is the only failing assertion; all other 10 assertions (schemaVersion, overall, generatedAtPresent, source, featureCount, totalsFeatures, hasLiveSource, hasNonUnknownFeatureData, snapshotUrl, maxAgeMinutes) are satisfied (evidenceItems: expected-output.contract).

sibling checks public-observability-page, public-models-page, and public-marketing-pages all passed with HTTP 200 responses, confirming the public website is reachable and the failure is isolated to snapshot freshness (evidenceItems: sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages).

source-context infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs lines 2168-2173: the runner fetches the snapshot via publicJsonUrl(args.publishedSnapshotUrl) and derives snapshotAgeMinutes from the payload, confirming the age value is read directly from the live published URL (evidenceItems: source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:2164-2172).
possibleCauses: Most likely: The GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the observability snapshot did not run or did not complete successfully within the last 715 minutes, leaving the previously published snapshot in place. The snapshot's source field is 'github-actions', confirming this workflow is the expected publisher.

Less likely: The workflow ran but failed to write or deploy the updated status.json to the GitHub Pages endpoint (https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json), so the stale file persisted.

Less likely: A GitHub Actions scheduling or quota issue (e.g., workflow disabled, branch protection, billing limit, or runner unavailability) prevented the workflow from being triggered during the expected window.

Least likely: A CDN or GitHub Pages caching layer is serving a stale version of status.json despite a successful workflow run having published a fresh file. This would be disproved if the raw file timestamp at the origin matches the stale age.

affectedAreas.reason: The snapshot's source field is 'github-actions', making the scheduled or triggered workflow that writes and deploys status.json the primary suspect for the staleness.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner: published-observability-snapshot probe
affectedAreas.reason: The runner branch at lines 2168-2173 fetches the live snapshot and derives snapshotAgeMinutes; if the age calculation is incorrect this could produce a false positive, though the structural evidence strongly supports a genuinely stale file.

affectedAreas.label: Eval contract: snapshotAgeMinutes assertion
affectedAreas.reason: The assertion { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } at line 482 is the violated contract boundary. The registry also defines staleAfterMinutes: 360 for this check, which is a separate registry-level threshold distinct from the contract's max of 300.

recommendedNextActions: Investigate the GitHub Actions workflow responsible for publishing https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json: check the Actions tab for failed, skipped, or missing runs in the last 12 hours and identify the root cause of the missed execution.
If the workflow failed, re-trigger it manually to publish a fresh snapshot and confirm the eval passes after the new file is deployed.

Audit the discrepancy between staleAfterMinutes=360 in infra/evals/status/features.json (line 383) and the contract assertion max=300 in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 482). Align these thresholds intentionally: if the workflow is expected to run every 5 hours, the contract max should be set to accommodate that cadence plus a buffer, or the workflow schedule should be tightened.

Add GitHub Actions workflow-level alerting (e.g., on-failure notifications or a status badge) for the snapshot-publishing job so that missed or failed runs are surfaced before the snapshot becomes stale enough to fail the eval.

Consider adding a follow-up eval that directly checks the GitHub Actions workflow run recency (last successful run timestamp) rather than relying solely on the published file's age, to catch workflow failures earlier in the pipeline.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: The registry sets staleAfterMinutes=360 for this check while the contract asserts maxAgeMinutes=300. Confirming whether these thresholds are intentionally different or represent a misconfiguration would clarify whether the contract bound is correctly set.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: features.json line 383 shows staleAfterMinutes=360; check-expectations.json line 482 shows max=300.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the GitHub Actions workflow run history shows a successful snapshot-publishing run within the last 300 minutes, the workflow itself is not the cause and a CDN/caching or deployment issue would need to be investigated.

If fetching https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json directly returns a file with a generatedAt timestamp less than 300 minutes ago, the snapshotAgeMinutes calculation in the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs) may be computing age incorrectly, making this a false-positive eval failure.

If re-running the eval immediately after this report returns snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300 without any workflow intervention, the failure was transient and may reflect a race condition or clock skew in the age calculation.
If no GitHub Actions workflow is configured to publish status.json on a schedule shorter than 300 minutes, the contract threshold may be misconfigured relative to the actual publishing cadence.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that checks the GitHub Actions workflow run history for the snapshot-publishing workflow and asserts that the last successful run completed within the expected schedule window (e.g., within the last 360 minutes), independent of the published file's age.
Add an eval that asserts the snapshotAgeMinutes value is below a warning threshold (e.g., 240 minutes) to provide earlier signal before the hard failure threshold of 300 minutes is breached.

Add an eval that validates the staleAfterMinutes registry value and the contract maxAgeMinutes assertion are consistent with each other, catching configuration drift between infra/evals/status/features.json and infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.

Add a GitHub Pages deployment freshness eval that checks the HTTP Last-Modified or ETag header of the published status.json URL to detect CDN or deployment caching issues independently of the file's internal timestamp.
